A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VIBE research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices A–K are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: v2 reports original VIBE experiments on CIFAR and ImageNet datasets, including defense comparisons, adaptive attacks, computational measurements, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds targeted-poisoning results and comparisons with post-training and detection defenses in Appendix I.

M1.justification: The EM procedure, optimal-transport E-step, posterior parameterizations, self-supervised initialization, and preprocessing algorithms are retained. The new detection evaluation reuses existing pseudolabels and preprocessing; no additional algorithmic step is specified.

E1.justification: Appendix I adds targeted poisoning aimed at misclassifying an individual test example through Witches Brew, and a distinct poisoned-sample detection task. These extend task requirements beyond the retained backdoor-resistant classification evaluations. No additional named dataset is established.

E2.justification: New Table 9 evaluates NAD and ANP against VIBE, with ANP reported only on CIFAR-10. New Table 10 adds SCP, citing SCALE-UP, plus BSU and PSBD. This introduces comparisons with two additional defense families while retaining the earlier comparator sets.

E3.justification: New Table 9 averages four attacks on CIFAR-10 and three on ImageNet-30, acknowledging the additional model and clean-data access assumed by post-training defenses. Table 10 introduces AUROC/TPR/FPR evaluation for detection. Existing benchmark protocols and training settings remain unchanged; detailed settings for the added tests are sparse.

E4.justification: The new Witches Brew test probes robustness to poisoning targeting an individual test example. Existing preprocessing ablations, adaptive and combined attacks, architecture comparisons, sensitivity analyses, and qualitative studies are retained without changed evidence.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains averaging over three runs and the stated variance bound of 0.2%. No new seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported. Table 9 averages across attacks, rather than introducing repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds the Witches Brew finding of ASR falling from 50% to 0% with VIBE and two complete comparison tables. Table 9 reports CIFAR-10 ACC/ASR of 94.1/1.7 for VIBE, 82.9/6.1 for NAD, and 90.9/2.1 for ANP. Table 10 adds detection outcomes, including VIBE BadNets AUROC/TPR/FPR of .99/.99/.01. Matched earlier results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Before Eq. 4, v3 corrects the definition of P by restoring x_i conditioning in p_theta(y_i|l,x_i). This resolves an inconsistency with Eq. 3 and Appendix A, which already included that dependence in v2. The remaining assumptions and derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same latent-label formulation, EM contribution, modularity, and broad robustness claims. The added appendix evidence does not redefine the central contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix I.4 now emphasizes robustness against LC even without preprocessing and removes the claimed BadNets improvement, consistent with unchanged Table 7 showing 0.4% ASR in both rows. Appendix I.6 additionally explains that successful poisoned-sample detection need not ensure a robust model after retraining.

D1.justification: Section 4 newly states that VIBE code is publicly available and supplies its repository address. Existing implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, runtime measurements, and baseline access information are retained.

R1.justification: Seven references are added, including Witches Brew, Poison Frogs, BSU, PSBD, and three training-time defense works. These modestly expand related-work coverage and support the new appendix comparisons; the central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds two appendix subsections, acknowledgments, and localized explanatory edits. The architecture subsection moves from I.5 to I.7 through renumbering. The main narrative and overall section organization remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Two comparison tables are added as Tables 9–10, shifting the numbering of later tables. Appendix reflow groups the sensitivity tables and moves Figure 9 to the final page; page-number footers are removed. All nine figures retain their original visual content.

improvement.justification: The probability-definition correction and revised preprocessing interpretation improve consistency, while the code address improves implementation access. Tables 9–10 provide evidence for comparisons with additional defense families. However, unspecified targeted-poisoning settings and detection thresholds limit the strength and reproducibility of the added evidence. The central method and existing results remain stable.
